content: The image shows a very young soybean seedling at the soil surface — one seedling appears to be struggling to emerge with a pale/bloated cotyledon, and there's a collapsed/dead brown seedling to the right. Soil appears wet/muddy. This points to pre/post-emergence damping off. Key candidates: **Pythium_damping_off** (water-soaked soft rot) or **Rhizoctonia** (dry, reddish-brown canker at soil line).

The Pythium reference collage is an almost exact match to the test image — same wet muddy soil, same pale/bloated cotyledons at the soil surface with struggling seedlings, and adjacent dead/brown seedlings. The Rhizoctonia reference shows reddish-brown dry cankers on more established plants, which is clearly different.

Fusarium shows root/stem rot on more mature plants with reddish-brown vascular discoloration — clearly not matching the seedling emergence scenario in the test image.

**Summary of evidence:**
- Very young seedling at/near soil line in wet muddy conditions
- Pale/bloated cotyledon, soft appearance (water-soaked)
- Dead/collapsed brown seedling adjacent — pre/post-emergence damping off
- Wet soil conditions typical of Pythium environment
- Reference images for Pythium_damping_off are nearly identical to the test image
